item.title: [LU-20683] UDSP does not import rules of priority 0
item.description:
`lnetctl udsp add` says it accepts priority values 0 or greater:

$ lnetctl udsp --help
udsp add: add a udsp
[...]
        --priority p:  Assign priority value p where p >= 0.
                       Note: 0 is the highest priority.

However, rules of priority value zero disappear when restarting lnet, such as after reboot. This is the content of /etc/lnet.conf:

net:
-     net type: o2ib
      local NI(s):
      -     interfaces:
                  0: ens11f0np0
            tunables:
                  peer_timeout: 180
                  peer_credits: 32
                  peer_buffer_credits: 0
                  credits: 1024
            lnd tunables:
                  peercredits_hiw: 16
                  concurrent_sends: 64
                  map_on_demand: true
                  fmr_pool_size: 2048
                  fmr_flush_trigger: 384
                  fmr_cache: 1
                  ntx: 2048
                  conns_per_peer: 4
                  tos: -1
            CPT: "[0,1]"
peer:
[...]
global:
    numa_range: 0
    max_interfaces: 200
    discovery: 1
    drop_asym_route: 0
    retry_count: 2
    transaction_timeout: 150
    health_sensitivity: 100
    recovery_interval: 1
    router_sensitivity: 100
    lnd_timeout: 49
    response_tracking: 3
    recovery_limit: 0
    max_recovery_ping_interval: 900
udsp:
    - idx: 0
      src: o2ib
      action:
          priority: 0
    - idx: 1
      dst: o2ib
      action:
          priority: 0

After restarting, lnetctl udsp show returns nothing. 

$ sudo systemctl start lnet
Job for lnet.service failed because the control process exited with error code.
See "systemctl status lnet.service" and "journalctl -xeu lnet.service" for details.
$ sudo journalctl -xeu lnet.service --no-pager

░░ Support: http://www.ubuntu.com/support

░░
░░ The job identifier is 1434.

Sep 02 06:57:04 [hostname] lnetctl[8844]: Ignoring unrecognized key 'ntx' for 'lnd tunables'

When I modified the priority to 1 instead of 0, the UDSP settings are properly loaded, and can be seen with `lnetctl udsp show`.
